scope.performance_numbers: No new per-stage or SQL timings measured. Peer acceptance_review owns original raw attribution.

conclusion: Yes: each original unscoped scale resume performs another complete source-tree metadata walk plus O(N) in-memory universe construction, even though at most 200 dependents are admitted in that invocation.

No: this does not imply a complete files/symbols SQLite load or full snapshot per resume. Validity-keyed file-state and resolver catalogs already avoid those loads; prepare_snapshot covers the current write_units.

The bounded dependency/surface queries explicitly enlarge their SQL prefix by completed.len and remove completed paths in Rust. Repeated resumes can therefore reread a growing completed prefix despite only emitting budget+1 new paths.

PR173, present in P59, removes redundant pending probes inside one prepare under a proven local window; it deliberately does not reuse that window across prepares or eliminate the growing-prefix cost.

Existing primary reverse access indexes are present. An imports covering-index enhancement and a frontier ownership-only move are finite optional candidates, not demonstrated fixes for 100k or substitutes for original workloads.

Do not skip scanning merely because the database has a pending frontier, or replace the original scale dispatch with changed_paths hints: that changes external-edit detection or the registered workload.

call_chain.fact: Every initial incremental and each resume calls build(aa,false,...); build uses backend.build_index_report(full).
build_index_report sends only {full}; event-scoped changed_paths is a separate API and is not used by this original scale loop.
Absent changed/removed lists become an empty BuildScope and then None.
run_split_build forwards scope unchanged to CodeIndex::prepare_build_scoped; stale prepared epoch retries the same original scope.
Capture prepared index epoch, perform scan/diff and CapturedProject::capture; these are included in scan_diff_ms.

evidence.fact: Only nonempty explicit scope selects scoped_scan_and_diff. Otherwise scan_with_manifest always runs, then full yielded_paths HashSet and diff over scanned entries; existing paths are iterated for removals.
Parallel ignore walk; each regular file pays metadata() for size/mtime. One shared walk replaces historical multiple walks, so do not claim three independent full walks.
Each scanned file is compared. Same size/mtime/current policies skips file bytes, so a metadata walk is not a claim of hashing every source file.
build_actions_map clones every admitted path into a new map, with parsed files Add/Update and remaining files Skip.
DirtyClosed::compute builds that full actions map before bounded dirty propagation.
Every capture clones scanned_paths into BTreeSet/FileCatalog, derives ancestor sets and config/manifest probes; config parsing itself has a cache.

confirmed_hotspots.complexity: For R unscoped resumes over N surviving files the walk/comparison and universe work is O(R*N), with ordered catalog insertion additionally dependent on sorting/collection implementation. This is a source-level bound, not elapsed attribution.
confirmed_hotspots.not_safe_shortcut: Pending frontier/unchanged DB generation proves nothing about unindexed filesystem changes between separate index calls.

counterexample_to_unconditional_resume_f.setup: Commit a partial dirty closure with some completed importers. Before the next ordinary index call, edit or remove a different provider, add a source file, or change .gitignore/tsconfig without writing the index DB.
counterexample_to_unconditional_resume_f.expected: The next original unscoped scan sees the new input, updates project-model evidence and rebases/clears completed where required.
counterexample_to_unconditional_resume_f.unsafe_result: A frontier-only fast path can miss the new invalidation or retain completed paths from the old basis. DB epoch need not move when source files are edited.

confirmed_hotspots.recommendation: Keep original unscoped scan semantics. A future full-walk-preserving optimization may reduce temporary path/catalog allocations, but no safe constant-time resume proof is present in this scope. Do not change the benchmark to scoped calls.

evidence.fact: cap=limit+1; probe_cap=cap+excluded.len; each (kind,keys batch) SELECT DISTINCT file_path ... ORDER BY file_path LIMIT probe_cap materializes String rows, then excluded is tested in Rust.
Same cap+excluded.len prefix for each of imports, symbol_refs and call_edges, with Rust exclusion; global BTreeSet retains the smallest cap distinct eligible paths.

State.completed is converted to exclusion collections and queries run afresh in each prepare. PR173 surface/dependency windows only serve that same prepare; changed seed basis or exceeded admission contract uses original fallback.
Durable frontier includes complete payload/digest, loaded and deserialized on each resume and serialized for a new pending frontier.
Frontier keeps full completed set under original MAX_FRONTIER_ENTRIES and MAX_FRONTIER_BYTES; storage validation is not optional.

confirmed_hotspots.complexity: For a stable single-key fanout with completed paths forming an ordered prefix, returned rows can grow roughly with completed length on every resume; over N/B batches this can approach O(N^2/B) returned-prefix work per applicable query. Multiple keys, duplicate rows, sort work and early caps depend on actual distribution; no measured VM total asserted.
confirmed_hotspots.not_proven: An SQL NOT IN/anti-join can reduce Rust row transfer but still inspect completed rows or build an exclusion set; it is not automatically an asymptotic SQLite improvement.

counterexample_to_max_completed_keyset.unsafe_filter: file_path > max(completed) loses still-unprocessed a.ts. Completed is not required to be an ordered prefix of each individual dependency/surface query.

confirmed_hotspots.further_counterexample: A newly rebound dependency, new root/facade seed or external writer between prepares invalidates an old query window; reuse must not rely solely on the prior local window or seed-symbol token, which is not a proof of all dependency/import/reference tables.
confirmed_hotspots.recommendation: Keep PR173's proven same-prepare window. Before any cross-prepare cursor/cache, establish exact query-basis validity and holes/late-write correctness; preserve budget+1 overflow witness, union ordering, all duplicate semantics, current transaction/epoch fence and durable complete set.

excluded_misdiagnoses.fact: get_file_state checks stored files_state aggregate and returns a shared Arc cache hit. SQL full load only on miss, with before/after token condition for warming.

Incremental writes carry the cache forward; when post token already matches, return before Arc::make_mut. Dirty-only units do not rewrite files rows. Do not assert every dirty-only resume clones the entire map.

Empty incremental batches skip persisted catalog; validated cross-build catalog is taken and delta-updated; full SQL seed load is fallback. Type catalog reuses prior contributions and hierarchy edges are batch-local.
prepare_snapshot sums/current route nodes/precompression over current write_units, not all DB rows.

public_surfaces package/file index and resolution_dependencies(kind,key,file_path), symbol_refs(target_file_path,file_path), call_edges(target_file_path,file_path) exist. imports has resolved_path single-column index.

optional_minimal_candidates.reasoning: previous has only these references plus resumed=previous.is_some(). That boolean is captured before the move. optional_minimal_candidates.relevant_existing_controls: Keep and run original reconcile window/dirty propagation/resume/rebase/external epoch controls if adopted. No new workload/budget or new framework is required.

optional_minimal_candidates.priority: small query-path hypothesis; require plan/work evidence before adoption
optional_minimal_candidates.proposal_sql: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_imports_resolved_file ON imports(resolved_path,file_path);
optional_minimal_candidates.reasoning: Current imports positive-binding SELECT returns file_path by resolved_path and orders distinct file_path. Unlike refs/calls, its existing reverse index is not covering. A composite index can cover the single-target ordered lookup without changing query semantics; multi-target queries can still require DISTINCT/ORDER BY work.
optional_minimal_candidates.rollout_boundary: Fresh schema plus current-schema idempotent physical-index maintenance are both required. index_migrate.rs:59–70 does NOT rerun FULL_SCHEMA_SQL on an already current DB; adding only the schema line would miss reopen/current installations. Do not change semantic schema version, logical rows, epoch, incarnation, OR REPLACE or FTS rowids.
optional_minimal_candidates.risks: Extra index build/disk/write maintenance; full staging temporarily drops indexes and must later recreate the new one. This does not remove completed-prefix scans and is not promised to improve wall time.
meaningful_validation_design: Compare exact old/new query output for duplicate imports, empty/NULL resolved paths, multiple target keys, non-prefix exclusions and overflow witness.
Inspect actual SQLite query plan and original SqlWork rows/fullscan/sort/VM metrics on representative fanout without changing the original production query or budget.
Prove same existing-schema open installs the index without row/epoch/incarnation changes; full/rebuild/incremental 15-table oracle equality remains the existing product requirement.
